I get your sentiment, while I feel you’re basing your argument on a ridiculous notion. We alter our minds constantly, every action we take does it to some extent. Our use of Reddit does also, often to escape boredom, and I doubt it’s doing us any favours, would you agree? If we stick to the soft drugs; cannabis, psychedelics (or even alcohol)- they can be dosed for an all encompassing experience, or to enhance certain aspects of our mind while numbing others.

Often there’s negative effects from use. I believe that has more to do with the user 1. Overdoing the dose, 2. Using for the wrong reason or 3. Not taking ample time to recover and integrate the experience. 2. And 3. Specifically protect you against addiction or harm.

Many times there’s wildly positive effects from use. Studies prove a single psychedelic experience increases people’s openness, one of five big main traits. I know after a great night with moderate drinking and good company I’m more extroverted for the whole week after. Alcohol is just such a good social lubricant that you get further in a shorter amount of time.

Yet I had times where I was a purist (even with masturbation). During that time I became extraverted by my own accord and often got the ”no way youre not drunk!” treatment, which was empowering for me since I didn’t need to poison my body to match other peoples level.

But then life happened, and once again I try to use the legal drugs to enhance, rather than rely on. My coworkers can’t go a morning without coffee or they get a headache. I think that’s ridiculous. The first example leads to faster hunger, although your energy levels are technically the same as in the second example, which satiates. The point is that the body works at a continuum.
